summary: Foro público de jornada completa convocado por la Disclosure Foundation el 25 de junio de 2026 en el Kennedy Caucus Room del Russell Senate Office Building, Washington D.C. Bajo el lema 'Humanity at the Edge of Discovery', reunió a seis legisladores en ejercicio —los senadores Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) y Mike Rounds (R-SD), autores de las principales provisiones UAP en el NDAA, y los representantes Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), Eric Burlison (R-MO), Tim Burchett (R-TN) y Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA)— junto a Christopher Mellon (ex vicesecretario adjunto de Defensa para Inteligencia), Avi Loeb (Harvard, presidente del UAP Science Advisory Council de la Casa Blanca), el contralmirante (ret.) Tim Gallaudet, Harold Puthoff (EarthTech International, ex director del programa STARGATE de la CIA/DIA), el historiador Carlos Eire (Yale) y otros investigadores del MIT y la Harvard Kennedy School. Es el mayor ensamble público post-PURSUE de figuras legislativas, militares, de inteligencia y académicas sobre UAP desde los primeros releases del portal war.gov/ufo en mayo-junio 2026.
summary_en: Full-day public forum convened by the Disclosure Foundation on June 25, 2026 in the Kennedy Caucus Room of the Russell Senate Office Building, Washington D.C. Under the banner 'Humanity at the Edge of Discovery', it gathered six sitting legislators — Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Mike Rounds (R-SD), authors of the main UAP provisions in the NDAA, and Representatives Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), Eric Burlison (R-MO), Tim Burchett (R-TN) and Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA) — alongside Christopher Mellon (former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence), Avi Loeb (Harvard, chair of the White House UAP Science Advisory Council), retired Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, Harold Puthoff (EarthTech International, former director of the CIA/DIA STARGATE program), historian Carlos Eire (Yale), and researchers from MIT and the Harvard Kennedy School. It is the largest post-PURSUE public assembly of legislative, military, intelligence-legacy, and academic figures on UAP since the first releases of the war.gov/ufo portal in May–June 2026.
whatHappened:
El 25 de junio de 2026, la Disclosure Foundation —presidida por Christopher Mellon, ex vicesecretario adjunto de Defensa para Inteligencia en las administraciones Clinton y Bush— convocó el Disclosure Forum 2026 en el Kennedy Caucus Room del Russell Senate Office Building de Washington D.C., de 9:00 AM a 4:30 PM, abierto al público sin costo y transmitido en directo por el canal de YouTube de la organización. El foro se anunció oficialmente el 23 de junio de 2026 mediante comunicado de prensa en PR Newswire, con cobertura en NewsNation, The Hill y múltiples medios de defensa. El lema 'Humanity at the Edge of Discovery' estructuró paneles sobre seguridad y política, ciencia, transparencia gubernamental, y filosofía y religión.

La convocatoria reunió a seis legisladores de ambos partidos: los senadores Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) y Mike Rounds (R-SD), los dos senadores que han impulsado con más consistencia las provisiones UAP en el NDAA desde 2021 —incluyendo la enmienda UAP Disclosure Act introducida por Schumer, Rounds y Gillibrand que creó la UAP Records Collection bajo NARA Record Group 615 y fue parcialmente desmantelada en negociaciones legislativas—, junto a los representantes Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL, presidenta de la UAP Task Force en Oversight), Eric Burlison (R-MO), Tim Burchett (R-TN) y Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA). Los expertos incluyeron a Avi Loeb (Harvard, recientemente designado presidente del UAP Science Advisory Council de la Casa Blanca el 17 de junio de 2026), Harold Puthoff (EarthTech International, ex director científico del programa de visión remota STARGATE de la CIA/DIA en los 80-90 y figura central en los briefings informales al Congreso sobre programas de inteligencia UAP clasificados), el contralmirante (ret.) Timothy Gallaudet (ex administrador interino de la NOAA, quien ha declarado públicamente que los UAP son de origen no humano), y el historiador Carlos Eire (Yale, ganador del National Book Award, aportando perspectiva humanística sobre implicaciones filosóficas y religiosas). Se sumaron investigadores del MIT y la Harvard Kennedy School.

El contexto inmediato del foro es la tercera tanda del portal PURSUE (war.gov/ufo), publicada el 12 de junio de 2026 con 53 documentos, 10 renders digitales, seis videos y tres audios de NASA, y el informe del director de AARO Jon Kosloski del 5 de junio que reconoció que el 40% de los fenómenos reportados carecen de explicación razonable. La participación de Harold Puthoff es analíticamente notable: como ex director de STARGATE y figura vinculada a los briefings informales al Congreso sobre programas de recuperación clasificados (Skinwalker Ranch, AAWSAP/AATIP), su aparición en un foro público con senadores y representantes activos representa la integración más visible hasta la fecha de la corriente de inteligencia-legado con el ecosistema legislativo formal. La presencia simultánea de Loeb —que representa el eje científico-empírico— y Puthoff —que representa el eje de inteligencia-clasificada— en el mismo panel es la primera vez que ambas tradiciones comparten plataforma pública con legisladores activos en la era post-PURSUE.
whatHappened_en:
On June 25, 2026, the Disclosure Foundation — chaired by Christopher Mellon, former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence in the Clinton and Bush administrations — convened the Disclosure Forum 2026 in the Kennedy Caucus Room of the Russell Senate Office Building in Washington D.C., from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM, free and open to the public and livestreamed on the organization's YouTube channel. The forum was officially announced on June 23, 2026 via a press release on PR Newswire, with coverage in NewsNation, The Hill, and multiple defense media. The banner 'Humanity at the Edge of Discovery' structured panels on security and policy, science, governmental transparency, and philosophy and religion.

The gathering assembled six bipartisan legislators: Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Mike Rounds (R-SD) — the two senators who have most consistently advanced UAP provisions in the NDAA since 2021, including the UAP Disclosure Act amendment introduced by Schumer, Rounds, and Gillibrand that created the UAP Records Collection under NARA Record Group 615 and was partially gutted in legislative negotiations — alongside Representatives Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL, chair of the UAP Task Force in Oversight), Eric Burlison (R-MO), Tim Burchett (R-TN), and Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA). Expert speakers included Avi Loeb (Harvard, recently appointed as chair of the White House UAP Science Advisory Council on June 17, 2026), Harold Puthoff (EarthTech International, former scientific director of the CIA/DIA STARGATE remote-viewing program in the 1980s–90s and a central figure in informal Congressional briefings on classified UAP intelligence programs), retired Rear Admiral Timothy Gallaudet (former Acting NOAA Administrator, who has publicly stated that UAPs are of non-human origin), and historian Carlos Eire (Yale, National Book Award winner, contributing a humanistic perspective on philosophical and religious implications). Researchers from MIT and the Harvard Kennedy School also participated.

The immediate context for the forum is the third tranche of the PURSUE portal (war.gov/ufo), published on June 12, 2026 with 53 documents, 10 digital renderings, six videos and three NASA audio recordings, and the June 5 report by AARO director Jon Kosloski acknowledging that 40% of reported phenomena lack reasonable explanation. Harold Puthoff's participation is analytically notable: as former director of STARGATE and a figure linked to informal Congressional briefings on classified recovery programs (Skinwalker Ranch, AAWSAP/AATIP), his appearance at a public forum with active senators and representatives represents the most visible integration to date of the intelligence-legacy current with the formal legislative ecosystem. The simultaneous presence of Loeb — representing the scientific-empirical axis — and Puthoff — representing the classified-intelligence axis — on the same platform with active legislators is the first time both traditions have shared a public platform with sitting lawmakers in the post-PURSUE era.
whyMatters: El Disclosure Forum 2026 importa como nodo de convergencia institucional, no como nueva evidencia material. Ningún otro evento post-PURSUE 2026 había reunido simultáneamente las cuatro corrientes que estructuran el debate UAP en EE.UU.: la corriente legislativa (seis lawmakers de ambos partidos, incluyendo los dos senadores que redactaron las provisiones clave del NDAA), la corriente ejecutiva-científica (Loeb como presidente del UAP SAC de la Casa Blanca), la corriente de inteligencia-legado (Puthoff como ex director de STARGATE), y la corriente académica multidisciplinar (Harvard, Yale, MIT, Harvard Kennedy School). El Kennedy Caucus Room del Russell Senate Office Building —la misma sala usada para audiencias formales del Senado— es un marcador de legitimidad institucional: elegirlo sobre espacios civiles señala que el foro no es un evento de advocacy marginal sino una reunión de actores que gobiernan las instituciones que controlan la información UAP. El peso de Gillibrand y Rounds es particularmente relevante: ambos son los arquitectos legislativos del régimen de desclasificación UAP desde 2021. Su participación en un foro público implica que la vía legislativa y la vía de disclosure pública están siendo coordinadas deliberadamente, y que el foro funciona como un espacio de alineamiento de expectativas entre el Congreso y la red de advocacy. La participación de Puthoff es el elemento más informativo del epistemicStatus=developing: Puthoff ha afirmado en privado conocer la naturaleza de los programas clasificados; su aparición pública en este contexto, sin que esté bajo subpoena ni testimoniando bajo juramento, puede producir hints procesables que la posterior investigación contextualice. Analíticamente, el foro es la manifestación más estructurada del ecosistema de disclosure en lo que va de 2026 y anticipa la posible apertura de una nueva ronda legislativa de provisiones UAP en el NDAA FY2027.
whyMatters_en: The Disclosure Forum 2026 matters as an institutional convergence node, not as new material evidence. No other post-PURSUE 2026 event had simultaneously brought together the four currents that structure the UAP debate in the U.S.: the legislative current (six lawmakers from both parties, including the two senators who drafted the key NDAA provisions), the executive-scientific current (Loeb as chair of the White House UAP SAC), the intelligence-legacy current (Puthoff as former STARGATE director), and the multidisciplinary academic current (Harvard, Yale, MIT, Harvard Kennedy School). The Kennedy Caucus Room of the Russell Senate Office Building — the same room used for formal Senate hearings — is a marker of institutional legitimacy: choosing it over civilian spaces signals that the forum is not a marginal advocacy event but a gathering of actors who govern the institutions that control UAP information. The weight of Gillibrand and Rounds is particularly relevant: both are the legislative architects of the UAP declassification regime since 2021. Their participation in a public forum implies that the legislative pathway and the public disclosure pathway are being deliberately coordinated, and that the forum functions as an alignment space for expectations between Congress and the advocacy network. Puthoff's participation is the most informationally significant element of the epistemicStatus=developing: Puthoff has privately claimed to know the nature of classified programs; his public appearance in this context, without being under subpoena or testifying under oath, may produce actionable hints that subsequent investigation can contextualize. Analytically, the forum is the most structured manifestation of the disclosure ecosystem so far in 2026 and anticipates a possible new round of UAP legislative provisions in the FY2027 NDAA.
